_comment: docs/CONTRACTS.md §15: the scorecard `gnomon chaos --json` prints, schema gnomon.chaos/1,
and the enumerations it is scored with. A reader parses the card without reading the code,
so renaming a fault id, a schedule, a channel, a verdict or a key is a contract change.
packages/gnomon-core/src/chaos.test.ts asserts that the code's CHAOS_FAULTS ids,
CHAOS_SCHEDULES, CHAOS_TASKS and CHAOS_CHANNELS, the §15 fault table and this file are
the same sets, and validates a scorecard the real suite produced against the key lists.
Rule 6: these values are published here and by `gnomon chaos list --json`. They are not
added to `gnomon enumerations`, whose contract is the values a SURFACE may declare;
nothing in .gnomon/ selects a fault, a schedule or a channel.
No audit record kind and no degradation id was added with the suite. The one record
change that came with it is `verify` on a TaskRecord (see `task_record` below).

exit.1: one or more injected faults were silent
exit.2: the run is void: a negative control did not hold, the lane check failed, a clean run did not finish, or a planned fault never fired

task_record._why: TurnResult carried `verify` and runTask never copied it to the record, so `gnomon task --json` could not tell a check that failed every round from a clean pass. Present only when a declared check ran.
